[https://craiggoldman.house.gov/issues/cutting-taxes]
Cutting Taxes | Congressman Craig Goldman Skip to main content Cutting Taxes Image Legislation & Actions: Working Families Tax Cut – Signed into law Rep. Goldman voted for the Working Families Tax Cut, providing the largest tax relief in U.S. history, delivering tax cuts for families, small businesses, and seniors. H.J. Res. 35 – Signed into Law Rep. Goldman co-sponsored H.J. Res. 35, which repealed the natural gas tax imposed by the Biden Administration. The harmful gas tax policy increased energy costs for energy companies, thereby discouraging domestic energy production.   As a result of the tax on gas production, Americans paid more for gas at the pump. Don't Tax the American Dream Act – Introduced to the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is leading the Don’t Tax the American Dream Act, which would eliminate federal capital gains taxes on the sale of a primary residence after a homeowner has lived in the property for two years. PRECEPT Nurses Act – Introduced to the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the PRECEPT Nurses Act, creating a $2,000 tax credit for eligible nurse preceptors who mentor nursing students or new nurses in health professional shortage areas. No Tax on Takings Act – Introduced to the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the No Tax on Takings Act, ensuring homeowners and property owners are not taxed on gains when property is taken through eminent domain. Securing the Border | Congressman Craig Goldman Skip to main content Securing the Border Image Legislation & Actions: Working Families Tax Cut – Signed into law Rep. Goldman voted for the Working Families Tax Cut, which a llocates  nearly $150 billion for border security and deportation operations, funds border wall construction, and authorizes the hiring of 18,000 law enforcement officers.    HALT Fentanyl Act – Passed the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the HALT Fentanyl Act to permanently classify fentanyl as a Schedule I controlled substance, strengthening law enforcement tools and improving information sharing to combat the fentanyl crisis. Reimbursing Texans for Funding Border Security Rep. Goldman is working with Rep. Pfluger, Sen. Cornyn, Sen. Cruz, and all Texas Republican colleagues in calling on the federal government to reimburse $11.1 billion to Texas taxpayers for spending used to secure the border while the Biden administration failed to act. State Border Security Assistance Act – Introduced to the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the State Border Security Assistance Act to reimburse Texas for border security costs through federal legislation. Repealing Red Tape | Congressman Craig Goldman Skip to main content Repealing Red Tape Image Legislation & Actions: H.J. Res. 75 – Signed into law Rep. Goldman led the H.J. Res. 75, which repealed several burdensome Biden-era regulations on commercial refrigerators that would have forced manufacturers and small businesses by requiring costly equipment redesigns and manufacturing upgrades. Homeowner Energy Freedom Act – Passed the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is leading the Homeowner Energy Freedom Act, which repeals costly green energy mandates imposed on home appliances and new construction, reducing regulatory burdens that have driven up housing costs for American families. Streamlining Permitting to Enable Efficient Deployment (S.P.E.E.D.) for Broadband Infrastructure Act – Passed the House Energy and Commerce Committee Rep. Goldman’s broadband infrastructure policies—outlined in the Streamlining Permitting to Enable Efficient Deployment (S.P.E.E.D.) for Broadband Infrastructure Act—were incorporated into the Proportional Reviews for Broadband Deployment Act as part of a broader legislative package. These reforms eliminated duplicative red tape, streamlining project deployment and expanding internet access in rural areas and on military bases. Zero-Based Regulatory Budgeting to Unleash American Energy Act – Introduced in the U.S. House and U.S. Senate Rep. Goldman is partnering with Senator Jim Risch to lead the Zero-Based Regulatory Budgeting to Unleash American Energy Act. This bill would codify President Trump’s executive order requiring sunset clauses on energy regulations, ensuring that deregulation is the enduring federal standard. Burdensome federal government red tape has restricted energy production and increased the cost of energy for Americans. LIT (Liberating Incandescent Technology Act of 2025) Act – Introduced in the U.S. House and U.S. Senate Rep. Goldman is partnering with Senator Mike Lee to lead the LIT Act. This bill ends federal green energy restrictions on incandescent light bulbs, restores consumer choice, and eliminates government overreach into one of the most basic household decisions. Unleashing U.S. Energy | Congressman Craig Goldman Skip to main content Unleashing U.S. Energy Image Legislation & Actions: H.J. Res. 75 – Signed into Law Rep. Goldman co-sponsored H.J. Res. 75, which repealed the natural gas tax imposed by the Biden Administration. The harmful gas tax policy increased energy costs for energy companies, thereby discouraging domestic energy production.   As a result of the tax on gas production, Americans paid more for gas at the pump. Zero-Based Regulatory Budgeting to Unleash American Energy Act – Introduced in the U.S. House and U.S. Senate Rep. Goldman is partnering with Senator Jim Risch to lead the Zero-Based Regulatory Budgeting to Unleash American Energy Act. This bill would codify President Trump’s executive order requiring sunset clauses on energy regulations, ensuring that deregulation is the enduring federal standard. Repealing costly federal government red tape will unleash domestic energy production and lower energy costs for Americans. Working Families Tax Cut – Signed into law Rep. Goldman voted for the Working Families Tax Cut, which restored onshore oil and gas lease sales to boost domestic energy production, eliminate billions in subsidies for green energy initiatives, refill America's strategic energy reserves, and rescind the Biden Administration's electric vehicle mandates. Protecting American Energy Production Act – Passed the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the Protecting American Energy Production Act to prevent presidents from unilaterally banning hydraulic fracturing without congressional approval. Congress retains authority over fracking regulation, which has been vital to American energy independence. Advanced Transmission Technology to Reduce Rates Act  - Introduced to the U.S. House Rep. Goldman introduced the Advanced Transmission Technology to Reduce Rates Act to help modernize the electric grid and lower rates by improving access to advanced transmission tools, technical assistance, and information on grid projects. Improving Health Care | Congressman Craig Goldman Skip to main content Improving Health Care Image Legislation & Actions: Better Care, Better Cost Act  - Introduced to the U.S. House Rep. Goldman introduced the Better Care, Better Cost Act to strengthen Medicaid by rewarding health plans that provide better care at lower costs. This bill would help Medicaid patients choose higher-performing plans that would save taxpayers up to $9 billion annually .  Prior Authorization Accountability Act  - Introduced to the U.S. House  Rep. Goldman introduced the Prior Authorization Accountability Act, which would require insurance companies to disclose how often they deny patient claims before families sign up for a health plan.  Additionally, this bill would require insurers to report how often denied claims are appealed and overturned, and the average time it takes for appeals to be resolved. Working Families Tax Cut – Signed into law Rep. Goldman voted for the Working Families Tax Cut to establish the Rural Hospital Transformation Program, which invests $50 billion in rural hospitals. Additionally, it will remove individuals who are improperly enrolled in Medicaid, preserving resources for those who genuinely need them. The Rural Hospital Transformation Program will invest more than $1.4 billion in Texas’s rural health care over the next five years. These resources will strengthen and expand rural health care services for millions of Texans. More Affordable Care Act – Introduced into the U.S. House and U.S. Senate Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the More Affordable Care Act to help make health care in American more affordable for hardworking families. This bill would reduce costs, increase competition, and restore patient choice. Mikaela Naylon Give Kids a Chance Act – Passed the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the Mikaela Naylon Give Kids a Chance Act to improve pediatric cancer treatment by requiring pharmaceutical companies to study targeted therapies in children when scientifically appropriate. Additionally, it strengthens FDA enforcement and transparency. Improving Seniors' Timely Access to Care Act – Introduced to the U.S. House Re

Safeguarding Elections | Congressman Craig Goldman Skip to main content Safeguarding Elections Image Legislation and Actions: SAVE America Act – Passed the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the SAVE America Act to secure elections by ensuring that only Americans vote in America’s elections. This bill requires states to establish programs to identify and remove non-citizens from existing voter rolls. Fundamentally, it protects our most sacred right through common-sense requirements. Make Elections Great Again Act – Introduced into the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the Make Elections Great Again Act to set federal standards aimed at tightening election security and administration, focusing on voter identification, citizenship verification, stricter ballot rules, and limiting certain voting methods such as ranked-choice voting and universal mail voting. No Foreign Persons Administering Our Elections Act – Introduced into the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the No Foreign Persons Administering Our Elections Act to prohibit states and local jurisdictions from hiring non-citizens to administer federal elections. Backing Law Enforcement | Congressman Craig Goldman Skip to main content Backing Law Enforcement Image Backing Law Enforcement Officers Legislation & Actions: Laken Riley Act – Signed into law Rep. Goldman voted for the Laken Riley Act, requiring ICE to detain criminal illegal aliens, closing loopholes that allowed dangerous individuals to remain in communities after committing crimes. Working Families Tax Cut – Signed into law Rep. Goldman voted for the Working Families Tax Cut, which provides significant funding increases for federal, state, and local law enforcement. Stop Illegal Reentry Act of 2025 – Passed the U.S. House Rep. Goldman voted for the Stop Illegal Reentry Act of 2025, increasing penalties for illegal reentry after removal, including prison sentences of up to 5 years for first offenses, 10 years for offenders with a criminal history, and 20 years for aggravated felonies or repeat offenses. Uproot Rising International Students Engaged in Radical Subversion Act (UPRISERS Act) – Introduced to the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the UPRISERS Act, allowing the U.S. Secretary of State to revoke visas from foreign students convicted of assaulting police officers or participating in riots.  Priorities Working Families Tax Cut Uncovered: Wasteful Spending Back to top button

Goldman voted for the Federal Law Enforcement Officer Service Weapon Purchase Act, allowing retired federal law enforcement officers to purchase their service weapons upon retirement. FIREARM Act – Introduced into the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the FIREARM Act to protect gun store owners from overly burdensome federal regulations designed to restrict lawful firearm sales. Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act of 2025 – Introduced to the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act to establish a framework so that citizens can carry or possess concealed firearms across state lines. Ending Wasteful Spending | Congressman Craig Goldman Skip to main content Ending Wasteful Spending Image Legislation & Actions: H.J. Res. 75 – Signed into law Rep. Goldman led H.J. Res. 75, which repealed costly Biden-era regulations on commercial refrigerators that would have cost taxpayers more than $8 billion. Homeowner Energy Freedom Act – Passed the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is leading the Homeowner Energy Freedom Act, which rescinds roughly $300 million allocated to enforcing federal green energy mandates in new home construction. Working Families Tax Cut – Signed into law Rep. Goldman voted for the Working Families Tax Cut, eliminating more than $1.4 trillion in federal spending and ending Biden-era student loan repayment programs that shifted costs onto taxpayers. Recissions Act of 2025 – Signed into law Rep. Goldman voted for the Recissions Act of 2025, which cut $9 billion in spending from the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) and government funding for biased media outlets. Better Care, Better Cost Act  - Introduced to the U.S. House Rep. Goldman introduced the Better Care, Better Cost Act, which could save taxpayers up to $9 billion annually by implementing market-based incentives into the Medicaid auto-assignment process. Additionally, it could help ensure that patients receive improved healthcare as insurance companies are incentivized to provide better care to acquire more patients. ELITE (Eliminating Lavish Incentives to Electric) Vehicles Act    – Introduced into the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the ELITE Vehicles Act, ending federal electric vehicle tax credits and charging infrastructure subsidies, potentially saving taxpayers over $390 billion. Helping American Farmers | Congressman Craig Goldman Skip to main content Helping American Farmers Image Legislation & Actions: STOP Screwworms Act –  Introduced in the U.S. House  Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the STOP Screwworms Act to advance the production of sterile flies used to combat the New World Screwworm. This action is necessary to counter the devastating screwworm parasite that threatens livestock and would cause serious harm to American agriculture if left unchecked. New World Screwworm Preparedness Act of 2025 –  Introduced in the U.S. House Rep. Goldman is co-sponsoring the New World Screwworm Preparedness Act of 2025 to investigate and develop strategies to prevent potential outbreaks of the New World Screwworm. Working Families Tax Cut – Signed into law Rep. Goldman voted for the Working Families Tax Cut, which preserves the estate tax exemptions for family farms. With this policy, multi-generational agricultural operations can be passed down to children and grandchildren without being devastated by federal taxes.
